description: Synthetic operations and product datasets for 100 US retail stores (USR-001–USR-100). Store IDs and names align with scraped_100_reviews_news1.xlsx. Ops and product tables are generated (not scraped); reviews/news remain in the companion scrape file.
notes: Regenerate via: python scripts/generate_scraped_100_synthetic.py

description: Unique store identifier. Primary key for joining all tables.
notes: Matches store_catalog in scraped_100_reviews_news1.xlsx

description: Parent retail company or chain operating the store.
notes: Drives retailer-specific product templates and ops archetype

description: Customer-facing store banner or brand name shown on signage.
allowed_values: Usually same as retailer; may differ in multi-banner chains
notes: In this dataset banner equals retailer for all 100 stores

description: Human-readable store label combining banner and city.
notes: Denormalized on other sheets for Excel readability

description: US city where the store is located.
notes: Used for local context in news/reviews companion file

description: US state abbreviation for the store location.
Physical store format class affecting size, assortment depth, and ops scale.
notes: Supercenter → larger sq ft, more SKUs, higher labor hours

description: Foreign key to store_catalog.store_id.
notes: One row per store per week (52 weeks default)

description: Sunday date closing the retail week for which KPIs are reported.
notes: 52 consecutive weeks ending on or before generation date

description: Total store labor hours scheduled or worked in the week (all departments).
allowed_values: Positive; scales with store sq ft and format
notes: Supercenters ~2,800–3,600; neighborhood stores lower

description: Inventory shrink as a percentage of sales (theft, damage, admin error).
notes: Correlated with retailer archetype; higher in urban/express formats

description: Out-of-stock rate — share of tracked SKUs not available on shelf during the week.
notes: Lower is better; premium stores tend toward lower OOS

description: Share of online pickup / delivery orders fulfilled completely and on time.
notes: Applies to stores with online pickup capability

description: Count of formal customer complaints logged at the store during the week.
notes: Urban/high-traffic stores receive more complaints on average

description: Retail chain (denormalized).
Store name (denormalized).
Store city (denormalized).
Store state (denormalized).
Store format (denormalized).
Unique identifier for each field report or audit record.
notes: Primary key for this table

description: Foreign key to store_catalog.store_id.
notes: ~8–12 reports per store over 52 weeks (configurable)

description: Date the report was filed or the audit was conducted.
notes: Unstructured text suitable for ops-modality embeddings

description: Type of operational review that produced the report.
allowed_values: mystery_shop | safety_audit | inventory_audit | facilities | loss_prevention | district_visit

description: Business impact severity of the finding.
notes: Distribution: ~45% low, ~35% medium, ~20% high

description: Operational domain of the issue identified.
allowed_values: staffing | cleaning | equipment | inventory | safety | signage | planogram | shrink | customer_service
notes: Correlated with store OOS/shrink KPIs

description: Narrative description of the operational issue or audit finding.
example: Elevated shrink pattern detected near self-checkout area
allowed_values: Free text from controlled template set
notes: Key field for NLP / GPT summarization in StoreDNA pipeline

description: Remediation workflow status of the reported issue.
Role or function that submitted the report.
Retail chain (denormalized).
Store name (denormalized).
Store city (denormalized).
Store state (denormalized).
Store format (denormalized).
Unique product identifier within the store assortment.
notes: Sample SKUs only (~10–23 per store); not full catalog

description: Foreign key to store_catalog.store_id.
notes: Same store may appear on many SKU rows

description: Retail chain (denormalized); determines retailer-specific SKUs.
notes: Walmart gets Great Value/Marketside; Costco gets Kirkland, etc.

description: Store name (denormalized).
Store city (denormalized).
Store state (denormalized).
Merchandise category for the SKU.
allowed_values: Grocery | Dairy | Snacks | Beverages | Health & Beauty | Household | Fresh Produce | Frozen
notes: Maps to assortment_snapshot.category

description: Short commercial product title as shown on shelf tag or e-commerce.
notes: Includes retailer private-label names where applicable

description: Longer marketing or shelf-ready product description.
example: Store-brand vitamin D milk — everyday low price.
notes: Primary text for product-modality embeddings

description: Product attribute tags describing positioning and diet/format flags.
allowed_values: organic | premium | value | private_label | gluten_free | plant_based | seasonal (combinations)
notes: Pipe or comma separated in exports

description: Brand ownership classification for the SKU.
notes: private_label when attributes contain private_label tag

description: Whether the SKU was in stock at snapshot time.
notes: False probability tied to store oos_rate archetype

description: Relative price positioning band for the item.
notes: Derived from attributes; drives unit_price range

description: Synthetic shelf price in US dollars for one pack/unit.
notes: Not scraped; generated for demo only

description: Package size or count descriptor for the selling unit.
In-store location zone where the product is merchandised.
notes: Maps category to typical store layout

description: Number of shelf facings allocated to this SKU at the store.
notes: Supercenters tend toward more facings

description: Synthetic average weekly unit sales velocity for the SKU at this store.
notes: Value-tier items have higher velocity on average

description: Estimated gross margin percentage for the SKU (0–1).
notes: Private-label SKUs skew higher margin

description: Synthetic Universal Product Code (barcode) for the item.
notes: Not valid GS1 codes — demo only

description: Supplier or distribution center name fulfilling the SKU.
allowed_values: Retailer DC for private label; national/regional vendors otherwise
